title: What Leaders Can Learn From the College Football Quarterback Whisperer
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Using college football quarterback coach Eric Morris as its case study, this article extracts a leadership lesson from how he develops overlooked prospects like Baker Mayfield and Cam Ward into elite talents. Morris's method centers on asking players to explain why a play unfolded the way it did, training them to process fast-moving situations and see how the pieces fit together before executing. The author generalizes this into a broader leadership technique: ask team members what happened and why, rather than simply whether it worked, to build their ability to see the whole picture quickly. The piece frames this pattern-recognition skill as the precursor to real effectiveness.
points: Coach Eric Morris develops overlooked quarterback prospects by training them to process the field faster
His method: run a play, then ask the quarterback to explain why things happened the way they did
The goal is a football brain that processes fast, decides fast, and executes with confidence
Leaders can apply the same technique by asking What happened and why? rather than just judging outcomes
quotes: He coached a walk-on named Baker Mayfield, who dominated in college, won the Heisman Trophy, and now quarterbacks the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Morris knows how to take unheralded football prospects and mold them into top-tier quarterbacks.
He develops a player’s mental acuity to see the field, process defensive schemes, and adapt under pressure.
He believes that taking situations apart and examining every detail helps his quarterbacks to develop a “football brain,” the ability to process fast, decide fast, and execute with confidence.
This big-picture thinking is developed from dissecting many situations with two simple questions: “What is happening?” and “Why?
